newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa gets first online stockbroking service.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa gets first online stockbroking service.

text.p: South Africa this week got its first online stockbroking service and the organisers said they were pleased with the initial response.
Broker Martindale, Stacey and Du Toit (MST), which launched the service with online newspaper WOZA, said on Wednesday it had already signed up 55 clients.
"The response has been amazing. We have had a number of requests since Tuesday and have opened 55 new accounts," said WOZA Broking partner Paul Theron.
Orders are placed through E-mail via the WOZA domain on the Internet and executed by an MST broker on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's (JSE) Johannesburg Equities Trading (JET) system.
Theron said controls were in place to prevent abuse of the service including passwords and validation of user numbers.

MST has established itself as a leading discount broker since the deregulation of the JSE, which started last year. Theron said the online service would charge the same brokerage fees as for orders placed telephonically.
Company news and market reports are sent free of charge via E-mail to subscribers. Registered investors can also request live prices by E-mail from MST.
Demand for the service came from varying parts of the country including the major cities and far-flung rural towns, MST said.
